replication_question: Can EEG descriptors previously explored on propofol-sedation EEG (ds005620) generalize to an independent cohort with different hardware, montage, task, or acquisition protocol, without treating prediction as causation or consciousness evidence?

candidates.title: A repeated awakening study exploring the capacity of complexity measures to capture dreaming during propofol sedation
candidates.participants_stated: EEGDash catalog states 21 subjects. participants.tsv columns include excluded and bad_after_preprocessing; included count after those flags was not resolved from catalog text alone.
candidates.sessions_stated: OpenNeuro page tasks: awake, sed2, sed. Session count not stated on the catalog page inspected.
candidates.behavioral_labels: README describes repeated awakening / dreaming under propofol sedation. Exact event codes not inspected.
candidates.channel_montage_sampling: One inspected sidecar (sub-1010 task-awake acq-EC eeg.json) states SamplingFrequency 5000.0, EEGChannelCount 65, Manufacturer Brain Products, EEGReference n/a, PowerLineFrequency n/a. EEGDash catalog states 64 channels on some recordings and 65 on others, all 5000 Hz.
candidates.access_restrictions: OpenNeuro public download under CC0. Not permission to reidentify. Not redistributed here.
candidates.exclusions_or_missingness: participants.tsv has excluded and bad_after_preprocessing columns. Values not enumerated in this package.
candidates.compatibility: BIDS EEG. Compatible with a BIDS-aware importer only after checksummed acquisition under the repository bounded-access policy. Not a replication of itself.

candidates.title: Meditation vs thinking task
candidates.participants_stated: OpenNeuro catalog states 98 participants. A public comment on the same page reports that participants.tsv contains 24 HT, 31 CTR, 19 VIP, 20 SNY and 4 TM subjects, while earlier studies or source-folder TSV files mention at least 27 HT, 33 CTR, 20 VIP and 20 SNY (about 100). Conflict is flagged, not resolved.
candidates.behavioral_labels: README: four blocks, meditation and active thinking, eyes closed. First meditation block is breath counting for all; second is tradition-specific except controls. Groups include control and named traditions in the comment, not re-derived here.
candidates.channel_montage_sampling: Comment describes external electrodes (eye, mastoid, collarbone) and a replacement Fp1. Channel count and sampling rate were not stated on the catalog page inspected. Sampling rate left null.
candidates.access_restrictions: CC0 on OpenNeuro. Availability is not permission to redistribute derived claims as empirical confirmation.
candidates.exclusions_or_missingness: Participant-count conflict between catalog, comment, and cited earlier studies.
candidates.compatibility: BIDS EEG with task labels. Independent of ds005620 hardware (propofol Brain Products) and protocol.

candidates.title: The effects of sham hypnosis techniques
candidates.participants_stated: README and catalog state 52 participants (39 females).
candidates.behavioral_labels: 2x2 balanced placebo: conventional vs unconventional induction, framed as hypnosis or relaxation. Pre/post eyes-closed rest.
candidates.channel_montage_sampling: README: 64-channel EasyCap from Brain Products. Sampling rate not stated on the inspected README.
candidates.access_restrictions: CC0. Version pages inspected listed both v1.3.1 and v1.3.2; DOI pinned here to the v1.3.1 metadata page. Conflict flagged.
candidates.exclusions_or_missingness: A 2024 Scientific Reports paper states hypnotizability scores were available for only 83 percent of participants. Not re-derived from the TSV.
candidates.compatibility: Useful to test whether an EEG descriptor generalizes to a different altered-state construct. Not a propofol or meditation replication.
